{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart","additionalContext":"<MAKE_IT_SHIP>
Make It Ship is installed. Its skills are invoked with the Skill tool; when one applies to the request, invoke it BEFORE answering, even for a question that looks simple:
- /make-it-ship:ask — Make It Ship other-model advisors (absorbs OMC ask, ccg, omc interop; gstack codex, codex-probe, benchmark-models).
- /make-it-ship:browse — Make It Ship built-in browser - drive a real headless Chrome from Bash (mis browse) to QA web pages, take screenshots, check console/network/performance, compare screenshots, scrape page data into reusable browser skills, import your browser's cookies for a site (asks first) and open a visible Chrome with a side panel; no Playwright needed.
- /make-it-ship:cancel — Cancel Make It Ship modes - stops an active persistent loop, team workers and merge-readiness sessions and, only when the user asks, cancels the current run.
- /make-it-ship:debug — Make It Ship root-cause debugging on its own - reproduce, trace, test one hypothesis at a time (competing hypotheses in parallel tracer agents when several fit), record the root cause, then fix test-first.
- /make-it-ship:deploy — Make It Ship deploy (absorbs gstack setup-deploy, land-and-deploy, canary).
- /make-it-ship:design-images — Make It Ship AI design mockups (absorbs gstack design/ binary and the AI-variant part of design-shotgun) - generate, explore variants, iterate on feedback, evolve a screenshot, and compare them on a board in design/variants/.
- /make-it-ship:gbrain — Make It Ship gbrain integration, core flow (absorbs gstack setup-gbrain, sync-gbrain and the gstack-brain/gbrain helpers).
- /make-it-ship:help — Make It Ship quick help (absorbs Ponytail ponytail-help, ponytail-gain and OMC omc info, omc capabilities) - lists every mis command by group, skill, agent, keyword (including the ralph prefix rule), style level, MCP tool and hook, generated from the code; also versions and counts (mis info), the capabilities lockfile (mis capabilities) and measured results (mis gain).
- /make-it-ship:interview — Make It Ship requirements interview on its own - turns a vague request, idea or requirements doc into goal, constraints and testable acceptance criteria by asking only the high-impact questions, one at a time.
- /make-it-ship:ios — Make It Ship iOS on real devices (absorbs gstack ios-qa, ios-fix, ios-design-review, ios-sync, gstack-ios-qa-daemon, gstack-ios-qa-mint).
- /make-it-ship:loop — Make It Ship persistent mode (ralph/autopilot) - keeps working on a task until the run is reported with verdict VERIFIED, the run is BLOCKED for the user, or the iteration limit is hit.
- /make-it-ship:ops — Make It Ship operations helpers (absorbs OMC omc wait and omc mission-board, gstack landing-report and gstack-detach).
- /make-it-ship:pair-agent — Make It Ship pair-agent (absorbs gstack pair-agent) - let another AI agent drive this workspace's built-in browser through a token-protected endpoint, on this machine (--local) or through a tunnel (ngrok).
- /make-it-ship:plan — Make It Ship planning without building - turns a request, idea or spec into a written implementation plan (docs/make-it-ship/plans/<slug>.md) with tasks, acceptance criteria and verification commands, checked by mis plan check, and executable later with mis start --plan.
- /make-it-ship:plan-review — Make It Ship plan review on its own - the read-only critic challenges a plan or design doc (claims checked against code, pre-mortem, gaps, testability); on request also the CEO, design, developer-experience (DX) and engineering lenses (plan-ceo-review, plan-design-review, plan-devex-review, plan-eng-review) or autoplan, which runs all four with logged auto-decisions.
- /make-it-ship:qa — Make It Ship real-use QA on its own - detects the CLI, API, web (built-in browser, no Playwright needed), iOS (simulator; device via the debug bridge) surfaces, designs user scenarios, turns them into runnable qa-* checks, and reports BLOCKED where something cannot be exercised.
- /make-it-ship:reference — Make It Ship reference for delegation and orchestration (absorbs OMC omc-reference) - agent catalog, MCP tools, keyword triggers and hooks read live from the code, plus where the team pipeline, routing and commit rules live.
- /make-it-ship:research — Make It Ship research loops (absorbs OMC sciomc, scientist, autoresearch, self-improve and the omc autoresearch shim).
- /make-it-ship:resume — Resume interrupted work - a Make It Ship run after a crash, closed session, limit, or failure (re-checks what changed, which evidence went stale, what is still open), or, outside a run, a saved working context (branch, notes, uncommitted files) with a warning when the branch differs.
- /make-it-ship:retro — Make It Ship retrospective and project memory - machine-counted metrics from past runs and git history (commits, hotspots, per-author activity, reviewer hit rates), a few evidence-based habits, and durable learnings and decisions: search, distill notes into proposals, decision log with supersede, union merge for shared ledgers.
- /make-it-ship:review — Make It Ship code review on its own - read-only spec-compliance and quality reviews of the current changes (correctness, safety, tests, unneeded code or dependencies), each with blocking/major counts.
- /make-it-ship:run — Make It Ship main entry.
- /make-it-ship:session — Make It Ship project session manager (psm, absorbs OMC project-session-manager and Superpowers using-git-worktrees) - an isolated git worktree (and optional tmux session) per issue, pull request review, or feature, outside a Make It Ship run, with a baseline run of the quick checks.
- /make-it-ship:setup — Install, diagnose, update or remove Make It Ship - routes setup, doctor, MCP server setup, config, update and uninstall requests.
- /make-it-ship:ship — Make It Ship release preparation - docs and changelog, version bump (VERSION, package.json, CHANGELOG) with a v<version> PR title, diff scope and solo/team repo mode, a secret scan before push, a PR draft and release checklist from the verified run; finishing a branch (merge, PR, keep, discard) and tagging also work without a run, with the user's approval for any push, PR or tag.
- /make-it-ship:skill — Make It Ship learned-skill manager (absorbs OMC skill) - list, search, add, edit, remove and lint learned skills in the project (.make-it-ship/skills) or user (~/.make-it-ship/skills) location.
- /make-it-ship:skillify — Make It Ship skill extraction (absorbs OMC skillify and learner) - turns a repeatable workflow or a hard-won fix from the current session into a learned skill draft in .make-it-ship/skills or ~/.make-it-ship/skills, with triggers the prompt router matches.
- /make-it-ship:status — Show the current Make It Ship run - phase, tasks, required checks (PASS/FAIL/STALE/BLOCKED/MISSING), reviews, open questions, decisions needed, and the current verdict.
- /make-it-ship:style — Set the Make It Ship always-on coding style level - off, lite, full (default) or ultra (smallest complete change, reuse first, no speculative code).
- /make-it-ship:team — Make It Ship team pipeline (absorbs OMC team and omc-teams) - N workers on a shared task list through plan, exec, verify, fix with a bounded fix loop and mis evidence.
- /make-it-ship:telemetry — Make It Ship usage telemetry and analytics (absorbs gstack telemetry preamble, gstack-telemetry-log, gstack-telemetry-sync, gstack-analytics, community and security dashboards).
- /make-it-ship:writer-memory — Make It Ship writer memory (absorbs OMC writer-memory) - a story bible for fiction writers kept in .make-it-ship/writer-memory/memory.json - characters, relationships with their evolution, scenes, themes and world rules, with query, export and automatic backups.
- /make-it-ship:writing-skills — Make It Ship skill authoring, test-first (absorbs Superpowers writing-skills, its subagent testing method and render-graphs) - write a learned skill only after watching a subagent fail a scenario without it, then prove the subagent passes with it (mis skill test) and that it lints.

Always, in every task (not only inside a run):
- Unclear request: ask before building, one question at a time, only what changes the result.
- Code change: write a failing test first, watch it fail, then the minimal code, then the whole suite.
- Bug: find the root cause (reproduce, one hypothesis at a time) before changing code; never retry the same fix blindly.
- Done / passing / fixed: run the verification command and read its output first; report failures with the output.
- Review feedback: check each point against the code before applying it; push back with evidence when it is wrong.
- Independent work: hand separate tasks to subagents in parallel; keep authoring and reviewing in separate passes.
- Asking the user: restate the decision in one line, give your recommendation and why, then 2-4 concrete options (AskUserQuestion when available).
- Next step: when a piece of work ends, suggest in one line the one skill that fits next (after a fix /make-it-ship:review, before merging /make-it-ship:ship, a failing test /make-it-ship:debug); do not run it unasked.
</MAKE_IT_SHIP>

5. One line a reader gets at a glance? One line.

- New non-trivial logic leaves one small test or assert-based self-check.

**What this change does**: `cartTotal` now computes the discount as `Math.floor((subtotal * percent + 50) / 100)`, which rounds half up to the nearest cent. `lineTotal` and the no-discount path are unchanged.

**Must fix**: none.

**Should fix**: none.

**Nice to have**
- `/private/tmp/claude-501/m10-tmp/m10-mis-d-3-1792568719182/test/cart.test.js` checks only the exact-half case (1050 at 15% gives a discount of 158). A below-half and an above-half case would pin the boundary on both sides. Examples: subtotal 1049 at 15% gives 157.35, so a discount of 157. Subtotal 1051 at 15% gives 157.65, so a discount of 158. This is optional, because the existing test already fails without the `+ 50`.

**Lean**: nothing to remove. The diff is one expression, with no new dependencies, and the doc comment matches the behavior.

**Open questions**
- For integer cents and an integer percent, the arithmetic is exact, so `floor(x + 0.5)` is correct half-up. A fractional percent (for example 12.5) goes through floating point, so a value that should be exactly half could land just under it. This is low confidence. Nothing in the task or tests suggests fractional percents.
- Negative subtotals or discounts would round toward negative infinity. Nothing in the task suggests they occur.

**Not checked**: I did not run the tests. `mis check` handles that. I also did not review the untracked `docs/` and `.make-it-ship.json`.
